proofs.proof_tex:
Apply the all-dimensional adjugate-translation lemma with \(d=3\), \(S_d=S3\), and the polynomial \(P\) appearing here.  Its trace-pairing gradient and adjugate are exactly \(G_P\) and \(Q_P\) from the frozen definitions.  The hypothesis \(\det G_P\equiv0\) is the determinant hypothesis of that lemma; homogeneity is not needed for this step.  The lemma therefore gives
\[
 \mathrm dG_{P,X}\bigl(Q_P(X)\bigr)=0,
 \qquad
 Q_P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=Q_P(X),
 \qquad
 P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=P(X)
\]
for every \(X\in S3\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal T_P\), these are precisely the asserted identities.

Apply the all-dimensional positive-gradient kernel-rigidity theorem with \(d=3\), \(S_d=S3\), and \(C_d=C3\).  The present hypotheses say respectively that \(P\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\geq1\), that \(G_P\) is positive semidefinite on \(C3\), that \(\det G_P\equiv0\), and that \(G_P\) has rank \(3-1=2\) at \(X_0\in C3\).  The all-dimensional theorem consequently supplies \(u\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}\) with
\[
 G_P(X)u=0
\]
identically on \(S3\).  Its compression conclusion says, after an orthogonal change of coordinates sending the last coordinate vector to a multiple of \(u\), that \(P\) depends only on the symmetric compression to \(u^\perp\).  Since \(\dim u^\perp=2\), this is exactly one \(2\times2\) symmetric compression, as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(d\geq2\), let \(S_d=\operatorname{Sym}_{d}(\mathbb R)\), and let \(P:S_d\to\mathbb R\) be a polynomial, with no homogeneity assumption.  Define its trace-pairing gradient by \(\mathrm dP_X(H)=\operatorname{tr}\{G_P(X)H\}\), and put \(Q_P(X)=\operatorname{adj}G_P(X)\).  If \(\det G_P\equiv0\), then
\[
 \mathrm dG_{P,X}\bigl(Q_P(X)\bigr)=0.
\]
Moreover, for every \(X\in S_d\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 G_P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=G_P(X),\qquad
 Q_P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=Q_P(X),\qquad
 P\bigl(X+tQ_P(X)\bigr)=P(X).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(G=G_P\) and \(Q=Q_P\).  The trace pairing \((A,B)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(AB)\) is nondegenerate on \(S_d\).  Since \(G\) is the trace-pairing gradient of the polynomial \(P\), symmetry of the second derivative gives, for every \(H,J\in S_d\),
\[
 \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\mathrm dG_X(H)J\bigr)
 =\mathrm d^2P_X(H,J)
 =\mathrm d^2P_X(J,H)
 =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(H\,\mathrm dG_X(J)\bigr). \tag{1}
\]
In coordinates, (1) includes the half-weight convention for off-diagonal entries: differentiating with respect to the coordinate \(x_{ij}\), \(i<j\), gives twice the \((i,j)\) entry of the trace-pairing gradient.

For arbitrary square matrices \(A,B\), differentiation of the Leibniz formula for the determinant gives the polynomial identity
\[
 \mathrm d(\det)_A(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(A)B\bigr), \tag{2}
\]
including when \(A\) is singular.  Apply (2) to \(A=G(X)\), \(B=\mathrm dG_X(H)\).  The hypothesis \(\det G\equiv0\), followed by (1) with \(J=Q(X)\), yields
\[
 0=\mathrm d(\det G)_X(H)
 =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Q(X)\,\mathrm dG_X(H)\bigr)
 =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\mathrm dG_X(Q(X))H\bigr).
\]
Since this holds for every \(H\in S_d\), nondegeneracy of the trace pairing implies
\[
 \mathrm dG_X(Q(X))=0. \tag{3}
\]

Define the polynomial derivation \(\mathcal L\) by \((\mathcal Lh)(X)=\mathrm dh_X(Q(X))\), acting entrywise on matrix-valued polynomials.  Equation (3), the polynomial chain rule for the adjugate, and the identity \(GQ=(\det G)I_d\) give
\[
 \mathcal LG=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal LQ=\mathrm d(\operatorname{adj})_{G}(\mathcal LG)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal LP=\operatorname{tr}(GQ)=d\det G=0. \tag{4}
\]
For every scalar polynomial \(h\) and integer \(k\geq0\), induction using \(\mathcal LQ=0\) shows that
\[
 \mathcal L^kh(X)=\mathrm d^kh_X\bigl(Q(X),\ldots,Q(X)\bigr). \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, applying \(\mathcal L\) to the right side of (5) gives the next directional derivative, together with \(k\) terms each containing \(\mathrm dQ_X(Q(X))=\mathcal LQ(X)=0\).  Thus (4)--(5) imply that every positive-order directional derivative in the direction \(Q(X)\) vanishes for each entry of \(G\), each entry of \(Q\), and for \(P\).  Because these are polynomials, their Taylor series in that direction are finite.  Hence, for every real \(t\),
\[
 G(X+tQ(X))=G(X),
 \qquad
 Q(X+tQ(X))=Q(X),
 \qquad
 P(X+tQ(X))=P(X).
\]
This proves all assertions without a homogeneity hypothesis.
added_lemmas.justification: This dimension-free polynomial identity converts determinant singularity and symmetric-gradient integrability into exact finite adjugate-ray invariance without homogeneity.
added_lemmas.gap: De Bondt gives a general quasi-translation criterion, but does not derive this adjugate direction from the trace-pairing gradient of a scalar polynomial.
added_lemmas.consumer: The all-dimensional positive-gradient rigidity theorem uses the invariant ray through a corank-one positive-semidefinite gradient.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(d\geq2\), let \(S_d=\operatorname{Sym}_{d}(\mathbb R)\), and let \(C_d=\{X\in S_d:X\succ0\}\).  Suppose that \(P:S_d\to\mathbb R\) is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(r\geq1\), with trace-pairing gradient \(G_P\).  If \(G_P(X)\succeq0\) for every \(X\in C_d\), \(\det G_P\equiv0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}G_P(X_0)=d-1\) for some \(X_0\in C_d\), then there is \(u\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(G_P(X)u=0\) identically on \(S_d\).  After an orthogonal change of coordinates, \(P\) is a polynomial in the \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) symmetric compression to \(u^\perp\).  Consequently, under the first two displayed hypotheses, either this fixed-kernel conclusion holds or \(G_P\) has generic rank at most \(d-2\), in which case \(\operatorname{adj}G_P\equiv0\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(G=G_P\).  First we derive cone monotonicity.  If \(A,B\in C_d\) and \(B-A\succeq0\), convexity of \(C_d\), the fundamental theorem of calculus, and the gradient hypothesis give
\[
 P(B)-P(A)
 =\int_0^1\operatorname{tr}\bigl(G(A+s(B-A))(B-A)\bigr)\,\mathrm ds
 \geq0. \tag{6}
\]
Indeed, both matrices in the trace integrand are positive semidefinite, so the integrand equals the trace of a positive-semidefinite congruence and is nonnegative.

Choose \(X_0\in C_d\) with \(\operatorname{rank}G(X_0)=d-1\).  Positive semidefiniteness implies that the \(d-1\) nonzero eigenvalues of \(G(X_0)\) are positive.  Therefore, for a unit vector \(u\) spanning \(\ker G(X_0)\),
\[
 Q_P(X_0)=\operatorname{adj}G(X_0)=\kappa uu^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \kappa>0, \tag{7}
\]
where \(\kappa\) is the product of those nonzero eigenvalues.  The all-dimensional adjugate-translation lemma and the substitution of its scalar parameter by \(t/\kappa\) give
\[
 P(X_0+tuu^{\mathsf T})=P(X_0)
 \qquad(t\in\mathbb R). \tag{8}
\]

Fix an arbitrary \(X\in C_d\).  Since \(X_0\succ0\), the finite number
\[
 \rho=\lambda_{\max}\bigl(X_0^{-1/2}XX_0^{-1/2}\bigr)
\]
satisfies \(X\preceq\rho X_0\).  Choose \(R\geq\max\{1,\rho\}\).  For \(t\geq0\), the matrices \(X\), \(X+tuu^{\mathsf T}\), and \(RX_0+tuu^{\mathsf T}\) are positive definite, and
\[
 X\preceq X+tuu^{\mathsf T}\preceq RX_0+tuu^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Apply (6), then homogeneity of degree \(r\), and finally (8), to obtain the two-sided cone-order bound
\[
 P(X)
 \leq P(X+tuu^{\mathsf T})
 \leq P(RX_0+tuu^{\mathsf T})
 =R^rP\left(X_0+\frac{t}{R}uu^{\mathsf T}\right)
 =R^rP(X_0). \tag{9}
\]
Thus the real polynomial \(t\mapsto P(X+tuu^{\mathsf T})\) is bounded above and below on \([0,\infty)\).  A nonconstant real polynomial diverges to one of \(+\infty\) or \(-\infty\) according to its leading term, so it cannot have both bounds.  The polynomial is therefore constant.  Differentiating at \(t=0\) and using the trace-pairing gradient gives
\[
 0=\mathrm dP_X(uu^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{tr}\bigl(G(X)uu^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
 =u^{\mathsf T}G(X)u. \tag{10}
\]
Because \(G(X)\succeq0\), its positive-semidefinite square root exists, and (10) is \(\lVert G(X)^{1/2}u\rVert^2=0\).  Hence \(G(X)u=0\) for every \(X\in C_d\).  Each coordinate of the polynomial vector \(G(X)u\) vanishes on the nonempty open set \(C_d\), so the polynomial identity principle yields
\[
 G(X)u=0\qquad(X\in S_d). \tag{11}
\]

Choose an orthogonal matrix \(U\) with \(Ue_d=u\), replacing the unit representative of the kernel line if necessary, and define \(\widetilde P(Y)=P(UYU^{\mathsf T})\).  Its trace-pairing gradient is
\[
 G_{\widetilde P}(Y)=U^{\mathsf T}G(UYU^{\mathsf T})U.
\]
Equation (11) implies \(G_{\widetilde P}(Y)e_d=0\) identically.  Hence
\[
 \frac{\partial\widetilde P}{\partial y_{dd}}=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial\widetilde P}{\partial y_{id}}=2\bigl(G_{\widetilde P}\bigr)_{id}=0
 \quad(1\leq i<d), \tag{12}
\]
where the factor two is exactly the trace-pairing convention for an off-diagonal symmetric coordinate.  A polynomial whose partial derivatives in these variables vanish is independent of them.  Thus \(\widetilde P\), and hence \(P\) after the orthogonal change of coordinates, depends only on the symmetric compression to \(u^\perp\).

It remains to justify the stated dichotomy.  Retain gradient positivity and \(\det G\equiv0\), but suppose no point of \(C_d\) has rank \(d-1\).  If some \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor of \(G\) were a nonzero polynomial, its nonvanishing set would be dense and open in \(S_d\), and would therefore meet the nonempty open cone \(C_d\).  At such a point the rank would be at least \(d-1\), while \(\det G=0\) would make it exactly \(d-1\), a contradiction.  All \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minors consequently vanish identically.  Hence the generic rank is at most \(d-2\), and every entry of \(\operatorname{adj}G\), being a signed \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor, vanishes identically.  This proves the dichotomy and the theorem.

If no such point exists, every \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor vanishes identically; hence the generic rank is at most \(d-2\) and \(\operatorname{adj}G\equiv0\).  Thus the corank-one obstruction is closed in every dimension, and only the higher-corank branch remains.

prose_updates.tldr: The field-tier contribution remains a complete denominator audit for primitive coprime reduced rational causal certificates supported on three covariance variables. The rigidity mechanism is now proved in every matrix dimension on the corank-one branch: adjugate translation needs no homogeneity, and homogeneity plus positive-gradient cone order forces a fixed global kernel line and compression whenever the gradient has rank \(d-1\) somewhere in the positive-definite cone. This closes Tamano's mixed \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) branch without degree or nonresonance restrictions and isolates the higher-dimensional open problem to generic rank at most \(d-2\), where the adjugate vanishes. The resulting \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) classification and terminating rational recognizer decide exactly when a reduced half-trek or related certificate has one nested flag denominator; no full higher-dimensional converse or new coverage theorem is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Tamano leaves the arbitrary-degree mixed rank-two kernel line unresolved in \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\), and the all-dimensional converse assumes rather than derives a common invariant flag. The corank-one kernel obstruction can in fact be removed in every dimension, while the higher-corank branch remains open.
project_justification.niche: The operative algebraic condition is determinant singularity of the trace-pairing symmetric-gradient matrix. Hessian symmetry turns its adjugate into an exact polynomial translation direction in every dimension; positive-cone order then globalizes a corank-one null direction. Coordinate-Hessian geometry and homogeneous-cone automorphisms concern different matrices or stronger supplied structure.
project_justification.fill: The dimension-free rigidity theorem proves a fixed kernel line and compression for every positive-gradient corank-one branch. Its \(d=3\) specialization closes Tamano's remaining mixed branch, completes the nested-flag classification, and makes exact rational recognition and denominator-only Wishart pivot auditing exhaustive for qualifying three-direction primitive reduced rational certificates.

prose_updates.related_work: Tamano's Theorem 1 \cite{Tamano2026SelfNormalizing} proves all-dimensional flag-power sufficiency and the exact flag-power Wishart pivot. Theorem 3 proves the three-variable reduction, including determinant stripping, spectral reduction, and the pure branches, while Remark 4 isolates constancy of the mixed kernel line as the missing three-dimensional step. The present \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) theorem closes that branch, and the dimension-free extension additionally proves the fixed-kernel conclusion for every positive-gradient corank-one branch; it does not settle higher-corank branches or furnish a full all-dimensional converse. Tamano's Example 2 gives the background three-node front-door benchmark, with the reduced form in equation (22), the covariance functional \[\tau(\Sigma)=\frac{\sigma_{AM}(\sigma_{AA}\sigma_{MY}-\sigma_{AM}\sigma_{AY})}{\sigma_{AA}(\sigma_{AA}\sigma_{MM}-\sigma_{AM}^{2})}\] in equation (23), and the denominator identity \(D=\Delta_1\Delta_2\) and \(c=10\) in equation (24); Theorem 1 yields \(m=(2,1,0)\) and the denominator pivot \(D(\widehat\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\stackrel{d}{=}(\chi_n^2/n)^2(\chi_{n-1}^2/n)\). In that benchmark, \(\gamma\) is the reduced-form association generated by unobserved treatment--outcome confounding rather than a direct causal effect, and \(\tau=\alpha\beta\) is the total effect. These benchmark identities are cited background, not solve targets or new claims. Foygel--Draisma--Drton \cite{FoygelDraismaDrton2012HalfTrek} supplies the named family of rational linear-Gaussian causal certificates to which the denominator audit applies after primitive cancellation. García-Puente--Spielvogel--Sullivant \cite{GarciaPuenteSpielvogelSullivant2010ComputerAlgebra} motivates exact certificate-producing causal algebra, and Bareiss \cite{Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity} supplies exact elimination operations. De Bondt \cite{DeBondt2017QuasiTranslations} informs only the finite translation mechanism and does not derive the adjugate direction from a symmetric gradient. Ciliberto--Russo--Simis \cite{CilibertoRussoSimis2008Homaloidal} and Gondim--Russo \cite{GondimRusso2015CubicHessian} study coordinate Hessians, not the matrix-valued trace-pairing gradient used here. Faraut--Korányi \cite{FarautKoranyi1994SymmetricCones} contextualize nested determinant powers. Tunçel--Vandenberghe \cite{TuncelVandenberghe2023HomogeneousCones} derive recursive structures from homogeneous-cone automorphisms; this adjacent mechanism does not settle whether self-normalization alone forces a flag in the remaining higher-corank branch.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(S_d\), the trace-pairing gradient uses \((G_P)_{ij}=\tfrac12\partial P/\partial x_{ij}\) for \(i<j\). Polynomiality is essential: the smooth homogeneous Schur-complement function \(y+z-(u^2+v^2)/x\) has a positive-semidefinite rank-two gradient with a moving kernel. Positivity is also essential: \(xu+v^2\) has a singular polynomial gradient with a moving kernel but fails self-normalization. In generic corank at least two, every \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor and hence the adjugate vanish identically, so the present translation proof supplies no direction; no lower-cofactor replacement is proved.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The new results are dimension-free adjugate-translation invariance, all-dimensional positive-gradient corank-one kernel rigidity and compression, its \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) specialization, the explicit signed mixed-residue bridge, the unrestricted \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) converse, the rational recognizer, and the exhaustive reduced-denominator audit enabled by that converse. Tamano's flag sufficiency, spectral and determinant reductions, Wishart pivot, and front-door benchmark are cited background. The all-dimensional theorem removes only the corank-one kernel obstruction; it does not prove a complete invariant flag in the generic-rank-at-most-\(d-2\) branch and is not a full higher-dimensional converse. No exact interval, boundary-valid interval, efficiency statement, or coverage theorem for \(\tau\) follows without joint analysis of the numerator and its dependence on the denominator. No software integration, bit-complexity bound, or non-Gaussian inference is claimed.
